1.stem: The student wants to convey to a general reader why this innovation matters. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The new stabilizer is a sugar-based gel, and a vaccine mixed with it stays viable for six months at room temperature instead of having to be kept frozen at -20°C.
options.B: By keeping the vaccine stable at room temperature, the stabilizer could bring it to the roughly two-thirds of the world where reliable freezing is unavailable.
options.C: Normally the vaccine must be kept frozen at -20°C, a temperature that no ordinary refrigerator can reach and that many clinic freezers cannot hold steadily for long.
options.D: Keeping a vaccine frozen at -20°C requires costly equipment and an electricity supply that does not fail, which is what led the researchers to look for a stabilizer.

2.stem: The student wants to emphasize the practical application of the research. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: City engineers can make existing bike lanes safer by adding a fine-grit epoxy overlay, which cut falls on wet pavement by 41 percent and can be applied with the same trucks used for lane striping.
options.B: City engineers can make existing bike lanes safer by adding a textured thermoplastic coating, which shortened wet-pavement braking distances by about a third and costs roughly 15 percent less per kilometer than resurfacing.
options.C: City engineers can make existing bike lanes safer by adding a micro-grooved slurry seal, which cut rider-reported skid incidents by 39 percent and bonds directly to existing asphalt, so the old surface need not be removed.
options.D: City engineers can make existing bike lanes safer by adding a resin-bound quartz sealant, which cut winter crashes by 44 percent and cures in four hours so lanes reopen the same day.

7.stem: The student wants to convey why antibiotic resistance is a serious concern. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Antibiotic-resistant infections already cause an estimated 1.3 million deaths a year, and once-simple infections could again become deadly.
options.B: Certain strains of bacteria have evolved resistance to the antibiotics that doctors have prescribed most commonly for decades.
options.C: Overuse of antibiotics in farming, where whole herds of healthy livestock are dosed routinely as a precaution, accelerates the spread of resistant bacteria.
options.D: Few new classes of antibiotics have been developed since the 1980s, and most drugs in use today were introduced before then.

8.stem: The student wants to emphasize, for a general reader, why the discovery is significant. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Recovering and sequencing the ancient genetic material took the research team eight years of work, from the first attempts on the tooth to the finished sequence.
options.B: The genetic material the team analyzed was recovered from the tooth of a single mammoth, an animal that lived roughly 1.2 million years ago and left the tooth behind.
options.C: By recovering the oldest DNA ever found, more than doubling the previous record, the study opens the door to reading the genes of other ancient creatures.
options.D: Until this study, the oldest genetic material that anyone had ever managed to recover was roughly 700,000 years old, a record that had stood for a long time.

options.A: In Madrid, urban parks lowered the surrounding air temperature by about 2°C.
options.B: The cooling effect of tree canopy was strongest during heat waves.
options.C: Across all 12 cities in the review, denser tree canopy was consistently associated with cooler local temperatures, with reductions ranging from 1 to 5°C.
